findings.title: Task 7.4 rewrites the onboard body but there is no orbit-onboard delta, so the rewrite violates live baseline scenarios
findings.recommendation: Add a MODIFIED delta for orbit-onboard. Baseline `orbit/specs/orbit-onboard/spec.md:56` requires the Identity section to name `/orbit:review-external` among the editorial commands, and `:85` requires "the external-review loop is named (`/orbit:review-external`) ... a pointer to the `orbit-review-external` skill" — a skill task 6.3 retires. Executing 7.4 (merged invocation, 15-command table) makes the generated body contradict the unmodified baseline. Copy the two affected requirement blocks, re-anchor them to `/orbit:review --reviewer external` and the review skill's external-handoff reference, and stamp the fingerprints.

findings.title: orbit-run-summary-emit still normatively commands the retired standalone command to emit (T0 requirement + timing semantics untouched)
findings.recommendation: The delta modifies `Emit scope` and `Apply per-chunk-end emission` only. Baseline `orbit/specs/orbit-run-summary-emit/spec.md:386` ("`/orbit:review-external` SHALL emit `review-external-<TS>.json` at T0", scenario `:409` invoking `/orbit:review-external foo --as proposal`) and the one-shot list inside `Emit timing semantics` (`:94`) keep the retired invocation as the normative subject. Post-archive this directly contradicts the review-external delta's "standalone launcher and skill are RETIRED". Add MODIFIED blocks re-anchoring the emitter to the external-handoff branch / `orbit emit review-external` (command value stays frozen). Also note the capability Purpose headers (`orbit-run-summary-emit/spec.md:5`, `orbit-review-external/spec.md:5`) carry the retired invocation and won't be touched by requirement sync — plan their update at archive.

findings.title: Write gate as spec'd rejects architecture-mode review emits, which the review delta routes through the same surface
findings.recommendation: orbit-review's delta (specs/orbit-review/spec.md:48) requires architecture-mode summaries (`change: null`, `doc`, `mode: "architecture"`, `handoff` section) to be "composed and written by `orbit emit review`", but the write-gate requirement says review emits pass `orbit-report-rendering`'s strict internal normalizer — whose contract and implementation (src/core/report-render.ts:196-199 pins `mode` to `proposal|system`; spine check requires `change` to be a string) refuses exactly those emits. `--render` (defined as the `--report` render, a change-scoped surface) is also undefined for architecture mode. Resolve explicitly.

recommendation_options.label: Carve out architecture mode
recommendation_options.body: Specify that architecture-mode review emits pass the universal-spine + scorecard/rollup checks with `change: null` + required `doc` and the orbit-architect-owned `handoff` shape, and that `--render` is unavailable (or a no-op with a stderr note) for that mode.

recommendation_options.label: Extend the normalizer contract
recommendation_options.body: Add a MODIFIED block to orbit-report-rendering widening the strict internal normalizer to `mode: architecture` (nullable `change`, `doc`, `handoff` tolerated), and state that `--render` for architecture emits renders nothing until an architecture report surface exists.

findings.title: R-d-9(b)/(c) mechanization is partial and the reframing is nowhere recorded
findings.recommendation: The charter says D5 mechanizes R-d-9's clauses (b) and (c). The artifacts deliver (b) as the boot render (D-d5-6's deliberate generalization — per-emit `handoff` stays architect-only), and of (c)'s four-item checklist only residency sweep (layer 2) and the touchpoints map land; boot-chain currency and coverage-vs-charter have no home in the audit-drift delta. Either state the reframing explicitly in proposal/design ("boot render supersedes per-emit handoff generalization; (c) items 2–3 deferred to <named trigger>") and plan the arc-ruling amendment/status-log entry at archive, or extend the audit-drift delta to cover the missing checklist items.

findings.title: Exit criterion 1 requires a stated numeric reduction target; the artifacts carry only the "≈ halves" estimate
findings.recommendation: The charter's exit criterion 1 is "a stated reduction target picked at explore time — the criterion is a NUMBER hit, not 'smaller'". Neither explore.md nor the proposal states a target; task 7.3 records before/after measurements against the ~40.6k baseline but names no number to hit. State the target explicitly (e.g. "six-body resident total ≤ ~20k, per the inventory's halving estimate") in proposal/tasks so stage ratification has a checkable criterion.

findings.title: Design D1's next_recommended class lists contradict the spec, and archive's post-write recompute is undefined
findings.recommendation: Design D1 puts "explore boundary" in the POST-WRITE class and omits archive; the spec (orbit-emit-composition:88-92) puts explore's maturity grid in PRE-COMPUTABLE and lists archive as POST-WRITE. The spec is right (maturity is a function of explore.md, unchanged by the emit landing) — fix design D1. Then specify what POST-WRITE means for `orbit emit archive`: at emit time the change directory has moved to archive/, so "recompute the change status with the just-written file" has no live change to compute against (the baseline archive `next_recommended` is a canned string, arguably pre-computable). Name archive's recommendation source explicitly.

findings.title: Authoritative per-command payload list and unknown-field handling unspecified
findings.recommendation: The payload contract's field lists are "e.g." (non-authoritative), and rejection is specified only for engine-owned fields. A typo'd narrative key (`pases_run`) is undefined behavior: one implementer builds a per-command whitelist (unknown key rejected), another a blacklist (unknown keys silently pass into the record — defeating write-gate strictness). Specify: the engine owns an authoritative per-command payload-field table; unknown keys are rejected naming the key (or explicitly tolerated — pick one); the per-skill `references/run-summary-schema.md` payload lists MIRROR the engine table, never define it.

findings.title: files_touched underspecified: first-emit reference, timestamp-to-commit resolution, and uncommitted work
findings.recommendation: Three divergence points: (1) the FIRST apply emit has no "previous apply emit" — as written it always yields `null` for chunk 1; if unintended, name the change's first commit as the fallback reference. (2) Specify how a timestamp resolves to a commit (e.g. `git rev-list -1 --before=<ts> HEAD`). (3) Say whether uncommitted working-tree changes count — design D6 uses `<change-start>..HEAD` (committed only), yet apply sessions typically emit with uncommitted work, making a committed-only list plausibly wrong rather than null. A wrong-but-plausible list is the exact failure texture D5 exists to remove.

findings.title: "Strict readers reject loudly" contradicts orientation's documented silent-skip fault isolation
findings.recommendation: The crash story claims a spine-incomplete emit is rejected loudly downstream, but the D3 orientation contract excludes spine-invalid emits from WAITING/LAST silently (fault isolation, exit 0), and gate trail reading is tolerant — a crashed post-write emit would quietly vanish from arithmetic, not fail loudly (only the report renderer is strict, and only if someone renders that file). Either specify that status/boot surface spine-incomplete trail files as a degraded line (detection without failure), or soften the spec's claim and name the actual detection path.

findings.title: models: map key vocabulary undefined and the design's own example matches neither phase nor slot names
findings.recommendation: The gates delta hooks hints to "the canonical-next command's phase or cadence slot" but never enumerates valid keys. The design example key `review-external` matches neither the schema phase names (`review-proposal`, `apply`, `review-system`) nor the cadence slot names the engine uses (gates.ts: `in-context`, `fresh`/`independent`, `external`), while the gates scenario says "maps the external slot". Define the exact key set (phases + slots), the precedence when both have entries, and fix the example key.

findings.title: CLI channel for doc-scoped emits and scope-resolution errors unspecified
findings.recommendation: The surface signature is `orbit emit <command> --change <name>`, but architecture-scoped emits need `change: null` plus `doc` — the spec never says how `doc` arrives (a `--doc` flag? payload field? is `--change` forbidden there?). Similarly `--change` doubles as an exploration name for `orbit emit explore` (explorations aren't changes), and the error path for a `--change`/exploration name that resolves to nothing on disk is unspecified (contrast: unknown command IS specified). Add the flag/payload contract for `doc`, the explore-name semantics, and the nonexistent-target error.

findings.title: Apply final_assessment stays payload-authored while restating engine-computed facts — the two-voices seam survives in the canonical example
findings.recommendation: The workflow-kind example's `final_assessment` ("Completed chunk 2 of 5 (inventory+parsing); 28 of 76 tasks done.") restates `chunk`, `chunk_name`, `tasks_completed` — all engine-computed extensions — yet for apply the field is narrative payload, so the payload can assert counts the engine's fields contradict. That violates D-d5-1's own governing rule inside the change's flagship example.

recommendation_options.label: Engine-compose the apply sentence
recommendation_options.body: Add apply's final_assessment to the deterministic-facts requirement (engine composes the chunk/counts sentence; payload may supply an optional narrative suffix).

recommendation_options.label: Write-gate consistency check
recommendation_options.body: Keep it payload-authored but have the write gate reject a final_assessment whose stated chunk/count tokens disagree with the computed extensions (the D4 cross-validation pattern).

recommendation_options.label: Prose rule only
recommendation_options.body: Specify that narrative fields must not restate computed extensions, and change the canonical example to a judgment-only sentence — accepting instruction-layer enforcement.

findings.title: orbit-conventions baselines still steer to the retired standalone invocation outside the delta set
findings.recommendation: Unmodified baseline requirements keep `/orbit:review-external` as a live invocation: `Review mode decision framework` (orbit/specs/orbit-conventions/spec.md:768, :783 — the third mode IS the retired command), the `Read-before-reference discipline` scenarios (:554, :564 — "about to invoke ... `/orbit:review-external`"), and the `.orbit-runs/` persistence scenario (:180). These are invocation references, not frozen record vocabulary. Add MODIFIED blocks (or fold into an existing one) updating them to `/orbit:review --reviewer external`, and stamp fingerprints.

findings.title: Explore counter entry grammar undefined
findings.recommendation: Define what the counter counts: top-level list items directly under `## Decisions` / `## Open questions` (nested bullets and paragraphs excluded), and the behavior when a section heading is absent entirely (0 vs. a malformed-format stderr note — d5's own consumed explore.md, with no Open questions section, is a live instance). Without this, two implementers count differently and the attestation loses its cross-check value.

findings.title: Chunk grammar cross-chunk coverage rules unstated
findings.recommendation: Contiguity WITHIN a declaration is specified, but not across declarations: overlapping ranges (chunk 1 groups 1-3, chunk 2 groups 3-4), gaps (a group covered by no chunk), or out-of-order chunk numbers. Now that the parser is engine-owned, state whether these are malformed (stderr warning + no-chunking fallback) or tolerated.

findings.title: Boot's "latest emit per mode" vocabulary undefined
findings.recommendation: "Mode" is a review-emit concept; say what the line covers — latest emit per review mode only, or latest per command family (apply, address-reviews, explore...)? A cold-start reader arguably needs the latest apply and address-reviews emits more than a per-review-mode list. Define the set explicitly.

findings.title: Exit criterion 3's mid-explore seam has no boot surface and no task exercises the cross-model boot test
findings.recommendation: `--boot` is change-scoped; the charter's boot test includes mid-explore, where no engine render exists. State in design/proposal how that seam is served (explore.md + trail emits as the file-resident boot material, or a follow-up extending `--boot` to explorations), and consider a 9.x task noting how criterion 3's every-seam pickup test will be exercised at ratification.

findings.title: Proposal's per-body token figures disagree with the cited inventory
findings.recommendation: Proposal says "address-reviews 9.9k, review 8.5k, explore 7.5k"; sketches/body-inventory.md says 9.8k, 8.3k, 7.1k (the 40.6k total matches). Align the proposal to the inventory's figures.

findings.title: Stray trailing space inside the Standing-recommendation literal
findings.recommendation: "`Standing recommendation: <the current leaning> `" carries a trailing space before the closing backtick — in a format-slot definition an emit parser may key on, the literal should be exact. Drop the space.

findings.title: The change's own explore.md omits the Open questions section the change makes mandatory
findings.recommendation: The consumed explore.md has four sections (no `## Open questions`), while the deltas harden the fixed five-section format, and D-d5-8's "this exploration practiced it" is vacuous with zero open-question entries. Restore the empty `## Open questions` heading for format compliance (it is also the live grammar edge case for the counter) and soften the practiced-it claim to cite the 2026-07-09 charter-era practice instead.

commentary: The artifacts are strong where the exploration looked: the new surface's happy path, the record-vocabulary freeze, and the MODIFIED blocks (all byte-diffed clean against live baselines; fingerprints and strict validation both pass; the cited gates.ts lines and normalizer names are real). The findings cluster at three seams the delta set didn't walk to the end. First, the merge's blast radius: the freeze protects record NAMES, but several baselines outside the delta set use the retired invocation as a normative subject — onboard's pinned prose, run-summary-emit's T0 emitter, conventions' decision framework — so the retirement is currently specified in one file and contradicted in three others. Second, the emit surface's non-flagship branches: architecture-mode review emits collide with the reused strict normalizer, doc-scoped CLI channels are unnamed, archive's post-write recompute has no live change to recompute, and the crash story assumes loud readers the D3 fault-isolation contract deliberately made quiet. Third, the change's own governing rule applied to itself: apply's canonical final_assessment still hand-restates computed facts, and the design/spec disagree on which class explore and archive fall into. I probed codegen determinism hardest (payload authority, diff references, counter and chunk grammars, hint keys) because this stage's thesis is that prose ambiguity is where the failure class lives; the risk texture is wrong-but-plausible records from underspecified references, not missing machinery.
